title: Seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement
description: North Dakota requires sellers of residential real property to complete a Seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement. The statement covers structural systems, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, roof, foundation, water and sewer systems, environmental hazards, and other known material conditions. Must be delivered to the buyer before acceptance of the purchase agreement.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered before acceptance. Exemptions include foreclosure sales, estate sales, and transfers between family members.

title: Agency Disclosure
description: North Dakota licensees must provide a written agency disclosure at the first substantive contact with a buyer or seller. The disclosure must explain the types of brokerage services available (seller's agent, buyer's agent, dual agent). Dual agency requires written informed consent from all parties.

title: Flood Zone and Flood History Disclosure
description: North Dakota requires disclosure of flood zone status and any known flood history. Given North Dakota's significant flood risk (particularly along the Red River, Missouri River, and Souris River), sellers must disclose whether the property is located in a FEMA-designated flood zone and any prior flood damage. This is included in the seller disclosure form.

required_actions.note: Flood disclosure included on ND-SPCDS. Must indicate FEMA zone and prior flood events.
Flood insurance may be required for properties in Special Flood Hazard Areas.

title: Closing Type — Title Company / Escrow
description: North Dakota residential closings are typically handled by title companies. Attorney involvement is not required by statute. Title insurance is customary. Abstract companies and title insurance companies perform title searches and issue title insurance policies.

required_actions.note: Title company conducts closing. Attorney optional but available for complex transactions.

title: Oil, Gas, and Mineral Rights Disclosure
description: North Dakota, as a major oil-producing state (Bakken formation), requires disclosure of mineral rights status. Sellers must disclose whether mineral rights have been severed from the surface estate and whether any active oil or gas leases exist on the property. The Dormant Mineral Act allows surface owners to claim unused mineral rights after 20 years of non-use.

required_actions.note: Verify mineral rights status with ND Industrial Commission, Oil and Gas Division.
